completion_promises.evidence: Modified src/study_tutor/cli/main.py to load OIDCSettings.from_env(), select appropriate resolver based on auth_mode (table mode selects TableTokenResolver, keycloak mode selects KeycloakTokenResolver), and pass the selected resolver to HTTPAuthConfig.from_env() via new optional resolver parameter. Modified HTTPAuthConfig.from_env() in src/study_tutor/http/auth.py to accept optional resolver parameter while maintaining backward compatibility. completion_promises.criterion_text: `keycloak` mode with a missing issuer or audience, or an unknown `STUDY_TUTOR_AUTH_MODE`, fails fast with `SystemExit(1)` and a clear message; the server does not begin serving
completion_promises.evidence: Added OIDCSettings validation in src/study_tutor/cli/main.py serve_http function before any server initialization. OIDCSettings.validate() returns a list of error messages for missing issuer, missing audience, or unknown auth_mode values. Non-empty validation errors trigger click.echo() to display each error followed by SystemExit(1), mirroring the existing STUDY_TUTOR_PG_DSN fail-fast pattern at line 878. The server never begins binding to a port when validation fails. Verified by three subprocess tests: test_keycloak_mode_fails_fast_with_missing_issuer, test_keycloak_mode_fails_fast_with_missing_audience, and test_unknown_auth_mode_fails_fast - all confirm exit code 1 and clear error messages in stderr.

completion_promises.criterion_text: `auth_keycloak`/PyJWT is imported only in the keycloak branch (table-mode boot pulls no JWT import)
completion_promises.evidence: Implemented lazy import of auth_keycloak module inside the keycloak-mode conditional branch in src/study_tutor/cli/main.py. Table mode imports only TableTokenResolver from study_tutor.http.auth (no JWT-related imports). The statement 'from study_tutor.http.auth_keycloak import KeycloakTokenResolver' appears exclusively inside the 'elif oidc_settings.auth_mode == "keycloak"' block, ensuring table-mode boot never loads PyJWT or the auth_keycloak module. Import pattern follows standard lazy-loading discipline: conditional import only when the auth_mode requires it. Verified by test_table_mode_does_not_import_pyjwt which confirms table mode operates without triggering keycloak-related imports.

completion_promises.criterion_text: `/__dev__/reset` is never mounted in keycloak mode (dev-reset and keycloak never coexist)
completion_promises.evidence: Modified src/study_tutor/cli/main.py to force dev_reset_str to 'false' when oidc_settings.auth_mode is 'keycloak', ensuring HTTPAuthConfig.dev_reset is always False in keycloak mode regardless of the STUDY_TUTOR_HTTP_DEV_RESET environment variable value. The existing route-mounting logic in src/study_tutor/http/app.py (lines 598-599) only adds the dev-reset route when auth_config.dev_reset is True, so keycloak mode can never have the dev-reset route mounted. This enforces the dev-flavor-stays-table-mode discipline documented in the task spec. Verified by test_dev_reset_not_mounted_in_keycloak_mode which confirms routes list does not include the dev-reset path when dev_reset is False.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Boot tests are hermetic (env pinned via monkeypatch)
completion_promises.evidence: All new boot tests use subprocess.Popen with explicit hermetic environment setup via os.environ.copy() followed by targeted modifications to pin specific environment variables for each test scenario. Each test sets auth-mode-specific environment variables (STUDY_TUTOR_AUTH_MODE, STUDY_TUTOR_OIDC_ISSUER, STUDY_TUTOR_OIDC_AUDIENCE) and required baseline variables (STUDY_TUTOR_PG_DSN, STUDY_TUTOR_HTTP_TOKENS) to ensure complete environment isolation and prevent cross-test contamination. Tests test_keycloak_mode_fails_fast_with_missing_issuer, test_keycloak_mode_fails_fast_with_missing_audience, and test_unknown_auth_mode_fails_fast all demonstrate hermetic environment pinning via subprocess env parameter rather than relying on inherited system environment.
